name: GA-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+27 partisan lean makes a Republican win structurally improbable
Hank Johnson is a long-serving incumbent running for renomination and reelection
Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 98%
Republican James Duffie shows no meaningful fundraising or outside support
model.rationale: The seat's D+27 lean, Johnson's incumbency, and a market price near 98% all point the same direction, and the Republican challenger shows no fundraising footprint to suggest an upset. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the expected margin stays near the district's structural lean.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal, health issue, or third-party complication involving Johnson would be the main route to a tighter race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Georgia's 4th District is one of the most Democratic-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of D+27, and Hank Johnson has held it since 2007. He is running again and was renominated without difficulty. His Republican challenger, James Duffie, has no reported fundraising and no outside spending on either side, leaving little sign of a competitive campaign infrastructure.

Prediction markets put Johnson's chances near 98%, and no general-election polls or expert ratings suggest the race is in doubt. The expected margin sits close to the district's structural lean, with wide uncertainty reflecting the absence of polling rather than any evidence of competitiveness. Barring an unforeseen development, Johnson is heavily favored to return to Congress for another term.
